proof_summary: For an arbitrary bound \(B\), set \(M=B+6\) and apply the hypothesis to \(n=M!/6=x+y\), obtaining primes \(p=6x-1\) (Sophie Germain) and \(q=6y+1\) (the upper member of a twin pair) with \(M!=p+q\). If \(p\le B\), then \(p\mid M!\) forces \(p\mid q\), while if the lower twin prime \(6y-1\le B\), then \(q\le M\) and \(q\mid M!\) forces \(q\mid p\); primality gives equality in either case, contradicting their residues \(-1\) and \(1\pmod 6\), so both sets are unbounded and hence infinite.
